status: Candidate-generation vocabulary, not proof of a historical relationship

matchingPolicy.normalization: Case-fold, collapse punctuation/space, preserve phrase boundaries. Never match inside larger unrelated words.
matchingPolicy.contentScope: Substantive prose only. Exclude global navigation, footers, table of contents, bibliography-only hits, build metadata and generated connections.
matchingPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each endpoint must contain an exact distinctive phrase in its title/summary or at least two substantive occurrences in its body. For cue groups require one match from every group in both endpoints. A single shared title-like specific work/person may support a 'shared subject' reading link, not a claim of influence.
matchingPolicy.strongRecommendation: For broader concepts require two independent specific topics shared or one specific topic plus two corroborating distinguishing phrases. Retain one exact excerpt from each endpoint. Do not pad to a target count.
matchingPolicy.labels: Use 'Shared subject' or 'Compare the question' for generated candidates. Use 'Historical influence', 'source', 'correction', 'refutation' or 'same person' only when explicitly established by the inspected text.
matchingPolicy.deduplication: Canonical target URL identity, not bare slug; the evidence-review Revelation article and archived conversation share a slug but are different pages.
matchingPolicy.direction: Preserve original relationship direction. A reciprocal discovery link is a comparison/cited-by route, not reciprocal endorsement.
matchingPolicy.groupCooccurrence: Every group cue must co-occur with the other groups in one substantive paragraph or a short window, not in disconnected portions of an entire article. Show support for all groups, not just the first generic term.
matchingPolicy.nonSubstantivePages: Exclude legacy generated cluster/repair notes and navigation/catalogue-only prose from semantic evidence. Retain registry entries without invented recommendations.
